title: State of Maharashtra v. Raman Raghav (Psycho Raman Murders)
crime_type: Serial Thrill Homicide / Nocturnal Blunt-Force Attacks
court_or_authority: High Court of Judicature at Bombay / Sessions Court Greater Bombay
legal_citation: Confirmation Case No. 12/1969; 1970 CriLJ 833; AIR 1970 Bom 242
source: High Court of Bombay Archives & Indian Kanoon (doc/612984)
ipc_sections: Section 84 IPC (Act of a person of unsound mind - Legal Insanity Defense)
Section 397 IPC (Robbery with attempt to cause death)
location: Suburban Mumbai & Central Railway track settlements, Maharashtra, India
evidence: Seizure of a custom heavy iron crowbar (bent rod) concealed in marsh bushes along the railway line matching cranial fracture patterns on 41 victims
Fingerprint impressions on oil lanterns and wooden cot frames matching police criminal record database records
Judicial confession recorded under Section 164 CrPC by Metropolitan Magistrate following recovery of victim umbrellas and stoves
Multi-session clinical examination report by Special Medical Board of three senior government psychiatrists
Bloodstained bush-shirt and trousers recovered from a washerman shack matching victim blood groups
modus_operandi: Prowled isolated suburban hutments, open shanties, construction sites, and railway line paths late at night. Identified defenseless individuals sleeping outdoors or in unlocked tin shacks. Without uttering a word, delivered crushing blows to the cranium with an iron rod, stole trifling items (currency coins, tea, umbrellas), and melted into suburban scrublands.
personality_disorder: Diagnosed by Special Medical Board: Chronic Paranoid Schizophrenia / Paraphrenia. Exhibited intense auditory hallucinations (hearing divine commands), persecutory delusions regarding occult powers, and complete absence of legal/moral insight into his crimes under Section 84 IPC jurisprudence.
common_traits: Nocturnal prowling along suburban railway tracks and impoverished hutments
Use of heavy blunt iron crowbar or fulcrum bar
Theft of minor, non-valuable domestic items
Impelled by systematized psychotic delusions and auditory hallucinations
summary: Historic Indian criminal jurisprudence trial. Raman Raghav was convicted of dozens of killings in 1960s Mumbai. The Bombay High Court commuted the death penalty to life imprisonment based on the Special Psychiatric Board finding that the accused suffered from chronic paranoid schizophrenia and was unfit to face capital execution.
